claim.quote: With the active veto, the average background rate in the crystal in the 1-6 keV energy region-of-interest (ROI) is $1.20\pm0.05$ counts/day/kg/keV, which is a breakthrough since the DAMA/LIBRA experiment.

key_value_text.quote: The amount of potassium contamination, determined by the direct counting of radioactive $^{40}$K, is found to be $2.2\pm1.5$ ppb, lowest ever achieved for NaI(Tl) crystals.
key_value_text.value: The amount of potassium contamination, determined by the direct counting of radioactive $^{40}$K, is found to be $2.2\pm1.5$ ppb, lowest ever achieved for NaI(Tl) crystals.

name: High sensitivity characterization of an ultra-high purity NaI(Tl) crystal scintillator with the SABRE proof-of-principle detector
notes: Recorded on SABRE North: the Proof-of-Principle phase is the first phase of that experiment.

summary.plain: A 3.4 kg sodium-iodide crystal in SABRE's test detector at Gran Sasso reached the lowest potassium contamination ever achieved for NaI(Tl) and a background of 1.20 counts/day/kg/keV in the 1-6 keV region, which the paper calls a breakthrough since DAMA/LIBRA.
summary.technical: Radiopurity measurement of crystal NaI-33 in the SABRE Proof-of-Principle detector (liquid-scintillator veto): 40K by direct counting 2.2 +- 1.5 ppb; 1-6 keV background 1.20 +- 0.05 cpd/kg/keV with the veto, dominated by 210Pb, about half of it in the PTFE reflector (Phys. Rev. D 104, L021302).

title: High sensitivity characterization of an ultra-high purity NaI(Tl) crystal scintillator with the SABRE proof-of-principle detector
why_it_matters: The paper presents these results as a benchmark for the next-generation NaI(Tl) detector arrays, such as SABRE North and South.
